title: On Standing at the gate for an hour
subtitle: 努力坚持 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）
meta: 主题语境：努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）　|　核心词汇：stand　|　正文 360 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 stand 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the engineer ① stood at the gate for an hour year after year, and every worker in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the engineer ② stands at the gate for an hour for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ stand at the gate for an hour at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ stood at the gate for an hour before — a line in the manual for April 1960 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Standing at the gate for an hour year after year, the engineer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ stand the noise for another night for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Stand the noise for another night at once and never mention it again.

By 1973 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the manual, and a new worker from the next workshop ⑧ stands the noise for another night year after year every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ stood at the gate for an hour again when nobody else would.

⑩ To stand at the gate for an hour, my mother said in 1978, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody stands at the gate for an hour for the whole place again and somebody must stand at the gate for an hour year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 站立（一般过去式 stood at the gate for an hour：1966 年工程师头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 站立（一般现在 stands at the gate for an hour：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 站立（不定式 to stand at the gate for an hour：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 站立（过去完成时 had stood at the gate for an hour：1960 年四月的说明书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 站立（动名词 standing at the gate for an hour 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 忍受（stand the noise for another night：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去忍受再忍一夜那种吵闹）
G. v. 忍受（stand the noise for another night：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 站立（后段两处：新来的工人照例 stands the noise for another night，而母亲又一次 stood at the gate for an hour）

answers.why: stand 意为“站立”，1966 年工程师年年地站立在门口站了一个钟头，那是车间里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 stood。
stand 意为“站立”，自那以后工程师替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 stands。
stand 意为“站立”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯站立在门口站了一个钟头”，此处为不定式 to stand at the gate for an hour。
stand 意为“站立”，说明书里 四月 那行字说明早在 1973 年之前就有人站立过，故用过去完成时 had stood。
stand 意为“站立”，工程师说“站立在门口站了一个钟头这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 standing at the gate for an hour 作主语。
stand 意为“忍受”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去忍受再忍一夜那种吵闹”，should ever 之后用原形 stand the noise for another night。
stand 意为“忍受”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻忍受再忍一夜那种吵闹（stand the noise for another night at once），以后再也不要提起。
stand 意为“站立”，新来的工人每个年头都照例忍受再忍一夜那种吵闹，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 stands。
stand 意为“站立”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地站立在门口站了一个钟头，用一般过去式 stood 叙述。
stand 意为“站立”，结尾那句是母亲 1978 年的话：要站立在门口站了一个钟头，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车间记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 stand 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1966 the engineer stood at the gate for an hour year after year, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the engineer stands at the gate for an hour for the whole place whenever the workshop asks.
Standing at the gate for an hour year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever stand the noise for another night for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next workshop stands the noise for another night year after year every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother stood at the gate for an hour again, and the workshop remembered that half.
